title: Should You Buy Nvidia Stock Before Aug. 26? Here's What History Suggests.
detail:
Should You Buy Nvidia Stock Before Aug. 26? Here's What History Suggests.
Adam Spatacco, The Motley Fool

NVDA
GOOG
META
AMZN
MSFT

Trading disclosure

Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) is scheduled to report its second-quarter fiscal 2027 results on Aug. 26, and the timing raises what has lately become a familiar question for Nvidia investors: Is the stock worth buying ahead of the earnings announcement?

The major artificial intelligence (AI) hyperscalers -- Alphabet, Meta Platforms, Amazon, Microsoft, and Oracle -- have already delivered their latest numbers, and a clear theme has emerged: Big tech continues to allocate substantial capital expenditures (capex) to expand AI infrastructure.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

This spending environment is constructive for Nvidia, which remains a primary supplier of data center GPUs while steadily deepening its position in CPUs, networking gear, and full-stack AI systems. With earnings right around the corner, the decision to buy shares now hinges on expectations, historical patterns, and a realistic view of timing.

Image source: Nvidia.
What does Wall Street expect for Nvidia's earnings?

Consensus estimates among Wall Street analysts point to revenue of roughly $91.8 billion, with a range spanning $90.3 billion to $96.7 billion. That figure is nearly double Nvidia's revenue from the second quarter one year ago. On the profitability side, analysts forecast earnings per share (EPS) of about $2.08, bookended by estimates between $2.03 and $2.20.

Wall Street's numbers are modestly above the guidance Nvidia's management provided when the company reported first-quarter results. Management previously stated that second-quarter revenue would be around $91 billion -- plus or minus 2% -- and projected gross margins near 75%.

How does Nvidia stock usually perform after earnings?

The chart offers a window into how Nvidia stock has behaved around earnings releases over the last year. Earnings reports are marked by the purple circles with "E" in the center.

Data by YCharts.

In the first instance, Nvidia stock was trading in the mid-$180s before reporting earnings. Shares subsequently slipped toward $170 in the weeks that followed before recovering.

The next release occurred after a run-up above $200. This was followed by a multi-week pullback into the $170 range. The most recent earnings event saw Nvidia stock peak above $220, followed by a prolonged sell-off that left shares currently near $207.

Across these episodes, the immediate post-earnings reaction has more often than not been neutral to negative over the immediate one to three months. That said, the longer-term trajectory has remained upward.

Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) stock might have slowed down in the past year, gaining less than 15% in the timespan, but the business is still moving at a staggering pace as it does its best to meet sky-high AI demand while investing in the bottlenecks in the buildout. Whether it's the desire to time a peak in hardware (no evidence of that yet), fears over circular financing and its potential to cause a violent unwind of some sort of "AI bubble," Nvidia stock isn't going to be right for everyone.

Perhaps the biggest reason to stay sidelined is the slowing upside momentum combined with the bearish bets put on by the great Dr. Michael Burry, who's best known for betting against the housing market ahead of the 2008 Great Financial Crisis. With Dr. Burry recently adding to his already lofty put position, questions linger as to whether Nvidia stock is peaking out, even as the business itself continues to post spectacular results.

pestoverde / Flickr

On the flip side, Dan Ives of Yorkville & Ives sees more wins coming for Nvidia, with "12-to-1" demand for its chips, a reality check that might not be baked into this increasingly skeptical market quite yet.

Act now: the analyst who called NVIDIA in 2010 just named his top 10 AI stocks — and Microsoft didn't make the cut. Grab the names FREE today.

Expectations are high, but Nvidia just keeps sprinting faster

Of course, it's going to be hard for Jensen Huang and company to keep sprinting at this pace for the long haul. Past blowout quarters have pretty much caused Nvidia's expectation treadmill to be on max. And while the firm hasn't broken a sweat just yet, skeptics like Dr. Burry know that staying at such a pace just isn't sustainable over time. But what if Nvidia really is a seasoned marathon runner that can keep the pace on a maxed-out treadmill for tens of miles more?

While the company itself is going to keep blowing the numbers away, what's harder to predict, at least in my view, is how investors and the market will react, especially as they grow more exhausted in a market environment that could become a whole lot more volatile as we head into the latter half of the third quarter — a period that tends to see things get just a bit more turbulent.

title: Oracle's AI Build-Out Is Squeezing Gross Margin, Not Its Valuation
detail:
Oracle's AI Build-Out Is Squeezing Gross Margin, Not Its Valuation
Trefis Team
Tue, August 4, 2026 at 7:25 AM PDT 3 min read
ORCL
^GSPC
ORCL-PD
MSFT
CRM
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Photo by TheDigitalArtist on Pixabay

The earnings multiple has come all the way down to the market's, while the build-out behind the story keeps pushing gross margin lower.

Oracle (ORCL) has given back about 44% of its value over the past year. The stock now trades at 23.9 times earnings, the same as the S&P 500, on an operating margin of 33% against 18.4% for the index. An average price on a well-above-average operating margin is the draw. What sits beneath it is changing: gross margin is stepping down.

The Mix Behind Gross Margin Is Moving Fast

Oracle Cloud applications produced $4.1 billion in fiscal Q4 2026, up 10%, and the cloud database business grew 29%. Cloud infrastructure revenue, meanwhile, grew 93%. Gross margin stepped down around 5 points across fiscal 2026, to roughly 66%, which management attributes to the infrastructure build-out and the accelerating revenue of that business. The fastest-growing part of the mix earns less than the rest today.

The Capital Budget Exceeds A Full Year Of Sales

Management has guided a net cash capital outlay of around $70 billion in fiscal 2027. Oracle booked $67.4 billion of revenue over the trailing twelve months, so the build-out will cost more in one fiscal year than the company sold in the previous four quarters. To fund it, the company expects to raise roughly $40 billion in debt and equity.

The Demand Is Contracted, The Cash Is Not

Remaining performance obligations, work signed but not delivered, ended fiscal 2026 at $638 billion, up 363%, and more than 1.2 gigawatts of capacity went to customers across that fiscal year. Most of the AI infrastructure contracts signed in fiscal Q4 2026 came as bring-your-own-hardware or prepaid deals, which the company says carry no margin penalty. The pressure is ramp timing and mix, not contract pricing: gross margin is guided down again in fiscal 2027. What has not arrived is cash: free cash flow over the trailing twelve months was negative.

Watch The Margin, Not The Multiple

The decision rests less on 23.9 times earnings than on whether infrastructure earns a margin like the rest of the company. If gross margin stops stepping down as the data centers reach full contractual revenue, the price is buying profits on the way; if it keeps sliding while fresh debt and equity fund the next round, it is buying revenue that costs too much to make. Oracle's record in market shocks is mixed: the stock fell 40% in the 2008 financial crisis against 53% for the S&P 500, and it fell further than the index in the 2022 inflation shock. The stock now sits 59% below its 52-week high, a deeper fall than in 2008. The trailing three-month drop came while the broader market rose, so the risk to watch is operational. For a scored view rather than an argued one, a five-factor scorecard ranks growth, margins, risk, cash and valuation.

title: How Much Upside Can ADBE Stock's Growth Deliver?

How Much Upside Can ADBE Stock's Growth Deliver?

The company long defined by its professional-grade creative tools is now pursuing a radically different customer. It is retooling its entire user acquisition model to serve billions of consumers through a freemium funnel. This strategic pivot is already showing results, nearly doubling its Creative Freemium monthly active users in the last year alone. The goal is no longer just power and precision for experts but mass adoption.

This top-of-funnel explosion is why the upside case hinges on revenue. The company is building a vast new audience to monetize over time, a strategy reflected in the faster growth of its business professionals and consumers segment. If this engine can convert even a fraction of its new users, the compounding effect on revenue will be significant.

That's the story. The cleanest way to interrogate it is to break the 3-year stock move in Adobe (ADBE) into the three things that can drive it: revenue compounding, net margin trajectory, and the multiple itself. Then look at which one is doing the heavy lifting under conservative assumptions.

The Three Levers Of Upside

Today's price is paying for some combination of these three. Under our conservative calibration:

Revenue compounding at 10.3% annually. Top line moves from $25.2B to $33.9B. Standalone contribution to the price move: 34%.

Net margin holds near 29%. Standalone contribution: -0.8%.

P/E multiple holds near today's 14.0x. Standalone contribution: 0.0%.

Multiplied through, the three combine to roughly 33% of upside over three years. Before we stress each one, here is the picture they are operating on top of:

What Happens To Upside If The Levers Change?

The base case lands at 33%. Soften revenue compounding by 200 basis points, so the top line grows at 8.3% instead of 10.3%, and the upside slides toward 26%. Holding net margin at its 3-year average of 28%, essentially where the base case puts it, leaves the upside near 31%. And stretching the horizon from 3 years to 5 lifts the upside to 62%, with the math compounding in the patient investor's favor.

What Could Tilt The Levers Higher

Beyond the freemium conversion, a new revenue stream is already taking shape. The company's AI-first products have seen a threefold year-over-year increase in annualized recurring revenue. This segment has already grown to greater than $500 million, providing a new layer of growth not yet fully priced into the base business.

Elon Musk became the world's first trillionaire earlier this year with the SpaceX IPO adding to his net wealth. While Musk's net worth has dropped with a declining stock price for both SpaceX and Tesla Inc, he remains head and shoulders above other billionaires.

Elon Musk Wealth vs. Larry Ellison Wealth

Over the last 12 months, only one man has been able to claim they were worth more than Musk. That title belongs to Oracle Corp co-founder Larry Ellison, who for one day in September 2025 was worth more than Musk.

A huge rise in the value of Oracle stock saw Ellison worth $400 billion, passing Musk's $385 billion net worth at the time.

The leaderboard change lasted only one day, with Musk the world's richest person for 364 of the 365 days in 2025.

While SpaceX and Tesla stock drops have taken Musk's wealth from $1.3 trillion to $702 billion, his net worth remains positive in 2026, and he is now significantly ahead of Ellison.

Musk ranks first overall at $702 billion, with a gain of $82.8 billion in 2026 according to Bloomberg. That gain also ranks first on the list.

Ranking first for the biggest net worth drop in 2026 is Ellison, who has lost $69.0 billion of his wealth this year. Ellison now ranks seventh on the billionaires list at $178 billion.

This means that Musk is now 4 times richer than Ellison, a far cry from being ranked behind the Oracle co-founder for one day last year.

Oracle stock is down 34% year-to-date in 2026 and down over 62% from its all-time high in September 2025.

Ellison and Musk are forever connected, with the Oracle co-founder previously serving on the electric vehicle company's board of directors and owning a stake in the company. Ellison's $1 billion investment in Tesla in 2018 served as a key financial commitment for the billionaire and the company at the time.

Trending: Avoid the #1 Investing Mistake: How Your 'Safe' Holdings Could Be Costing You Big Time

Musk's Net Worth History

Musk became a billionaire at the age of 41 and later became the world's richest person thanks to Tesla's share price.

A drop in Tesla's share price in 2022 took Musk's wealth down so much that he was awarded a Guinness World Record for the biggest one-year drop in net worth.

After being passed by Bernard Arnault and falling to the second-richest person in the world, Musk regained the title of richest man in the world in 2023 thanks to a recovery in Tesla's share price.
